CACHE WARNING: the URL SLUG SAYS "seven-killed" BUT THE LIVE HEADLINE SAYS NINE. The Guardian revised the death toll upward and kept the original slug. Do not take the figure from the URL.

HEADLINE AS PUBLISHED NOW: Nine killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan

DEATH TOLL PROGRESSION AND CONFLICT (do not average)
- NPR/AP, Friday (cache file MORN-GEO-NPR-jordan-church-shooting.txt): SEVEN killed, 40 wounded.
- Guardian, revised 24 Oct: NINE killed, 40 injured.
- Al Jazeera, 24 Oct, "Jordan's King Abdullah orders firm response after deadly church attack": notes "death toll now nine".
- ABC News index, labelled 14 hours before 08:35 GMT 25 Oct: "At least 9 dead, 34 injured in Jordan church shooting" — NINE dead but THIRTY-FOUR injured, against 40 from the Guardian and NPR.
- The 40-injured figure is attributed to Jordan's health minister. The 34 figure is ABC's, unattributed in the index.

CORE FACTS
- Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at St George's Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, Karak governorate, on Friday. Karak is about 90km (55 miles) south of Amman.
- Authorities described the attack as a terrorist act by extremists.
- Video aired on Jordan's state-owned Al-Mamlaka television, apparently from a security camera, showed three people firing at the church from a pavement and hiding behind trees and a low wall, then running towards the entrance. Reuters verified the video from the entry path and wall surrounding the church.
- Jordan declared three days of national mourning (Petra News Agency, via NPR/AP).
- Two of the wounded are in critical condition (Jordan's Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour, via NPR/AP).
- Security has been stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan, the US embassy in Amman said on Saturday.

NAMED QUOTES WITH EXACT ROLES
- King Abdullah II: "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation. Those who delude themselves into thinking they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity." He visited Karak hours after the attack and said perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist".
- Maj Gen Abdallah al-Maaytah, head of Jordan's Public Security Directorate, said most of those injured were receiving treatment and the hunt for the attackers was continuing.
- Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh said the attack had been carried out by "extremists" but it was too early to tell whether they had any links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.
- Prime Minister Jafar Hassan, on X: "This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and we will not allow society to go down this path."
- Priest Theodoros Soueiss: "A sense of panic took hold among those present. The gunfire was indiscriminate, and you never knew where a bullet might land."
- Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN, on X, described it as a "depraved and brutal attack on a house of worship".
- UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the violence, saying attacks against civilians and places of worship were unacceptable.

NO CLAIM OF RESPONSIBILITY has been reported. No arrests were confirmed in this copy.
